title: The pressure of ministry
scripture_text: “I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. Therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves. Be on your guard; you will be handed over to the local councils and be flogged in the synagogues. On my account you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles. But when they arrest you, do not worry about what to say or how to say it. At that time you will be given what to say, for it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you “Brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child; children will rebel against their parents and have them put to death. You will be hated by everyone because of me, but the one who stands firm to the end will be saved. When you are persecuted in one place, flee to another. Truly I tell you, you will not finish going through the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes. The student is not above the teacher, nor a servant above his master. It is enough for students to be like their teachers, and servants like their masters. If the head of the house has been called Beelzebul, how much more the members of his household! So do not be afraid of them, for there is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, or hidden that will not be made known. What I tell you in the dark, speak in the daylight; what is whispered in your ear, proclaim from the roofs. Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Rather, be afraid of the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell. Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground outside your Father’s care. And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So don’t be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows. “Whoever acknowledges me before others, I will also acknowledge before my Father in heaven. But whoever disowns me before others, I will disown before my Father in heaven. Do not suppose that I have come to bring peace to the earth. I did not come to bring peace, but a sword. For I have come to turn a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law—a man’s enemies will be the members of his own household. Anyone who loves their father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; anyone who loves their son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me. Whoever does not take up their cross and follow me is not worthy of me. Whoever finds their life will lose it, and whoever loses their life for my sake will find it. Anyone who welcomes you welcomes me, and anyone who welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me. Whoever welcomes a prophet as a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and whoever welcomes a righteous person as a righteous person will receive a righteous person’s reward. And if anyone gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones who is my disciple, truly I tell you, that person will certainly not lose their reward.”
devotional:
Jesus continues by laying down a number of facts in relation to persecution.

Persecution from without will never hinder the ministry Jesus has called us to, if we are allowing the Holy Spirit to work within us.

"Be on your guard against men; they will hand you over to the local councils and flog you in their synagogues. On my account you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles. But when they arrest you, do not worry about what to say or how to say it. At that time you will be given what to say, for it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.’

How do you think these disciples felt when they heard Jesus say this?

They were probably afraid and apprehensive and it would only have been through the power of the Holy Spirit in their lives that they would have been able to stand before antagonistic authorities.

Do not worry.

There are a number of problems with understanding of this verse, and on a superficial reading you could think that Jesus was being to idealistic. Do not worry about what to say. This is an opportunity to witness before governors and kings.

When Jesus tells them do not worry, He is not giving them a command, nor is he telling to live in denial. This is not a call to be brave, or to be strong, or to clench your fists, grit your teeth, put your heads down and suffer, no matter what. (This kind of approach to persecution will ensure that we will not be able to cope.)

However, it is a call to be dependent, to find your security in your relationship with God. It is an opportunity to allow the Holy Spirit to work in you. but he is saying that when we have hearts that are free, and when we are wise and innocent, then we will be less inclined to worry.

What kind of person would not worry under such circumstances?

Someone who has understood everything Jesus has said up to this point, someone that is finding his or her life in God. But if we are not free on inside, then we will feel threatened, and we will worry, wanting to preserve the freedom we think we have.

So when Jesus tells us “freely you have received, freely give,” He knows that being free on the inside, and presenting the Gospel as a free gift, will have a huge affect on how we will respond to persecution.

Do witness, but do it because you are free.

But there is another problem. When any one is brought before a local council, a governor, or kings, especially in the days of Jesus, you knew at least you could be flogged or even lose your life. Nothing in our natural lives will feel the desire to witness. So is Jesus being naive, or even cruel, expecting his disciples to witness before oppressive tyrants?

So how are we to understand this?

For in verse 20 he says “But when they arrest you, do not worry about what to say or how to say it. At that time you will be given what to say, for it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.”

What Jesus is saying here is dynamic.

Many people see this verse, as Jesus seeing persecution as an opportunity for witnessing. But this is to miss the point. The witness we give is more about what we are not what we say. The witness we give has more to do with how we respond to the persecution, not in how we defend ourselves from the persecution, or challenge the persecution. The witness we give is the result of God working in us, not us trying to be strong, or have answers, or learning the latest method of spiritual self-defence.

If, “freely you have received, freely give,” is true about our hearts, then witnessing will be just spontaneous. Standing before a court, will never threaten the freedom of a Christian. However, if we are not free, then we will see witnessing as a rule, something we feel we have to do.

We could even think that because we witness, and made a stand, and shared or faith, then God will be glorified. But God is only glorified if we witness from a posture of freedom and dependence.

We could even witness in these kinds of circumstances as an attempt to get free, not because we are free.

A. The answer to persecution is not to see the persecution stop, but the life of the Spirit in the believer. It is more important to react to pressure in the Spirit than see the source of the pressure removed.

B. The biggest threat to the work of God does not come from the pressure from without, but lack of the life of the spirit in the life of the believer.

C. Be more concerned about your dependence on God, and the work of the Holy Spirit in your life, than about and persecution you may face.

Sometimes the Holy Spirit will tell you to say nothing.

Sometimes our reaction and our calmness can say more than any words we might use.
prayer: Father help me to face all of life through the power of the Spirit.
